headline: WHO says it cannot fully assess a suspected plague death in Russia
headline_short: WHO cannot assess suspected Russian plague death
deck: Moscow says the Siberian laboratory worker died of pneumonia; America and the WHO want answers about a second case.
standard: The World Health Organization cannot fully assess the risk from a suspected plague death in Russia. 'We do not yet have the full picture,' Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, its head, said on Wednesday.

Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old technician at an anti-plague laboratory in Siberia's Irkutsk region, died last week. Russia says she died of pneumonia of unknown cause; unnamed sources told local media she may have caught plague from a broken test tube.

The WHO and America want answers about a second laboratory worker reported to have pneumonia. Dmitry Peskov, the Russian president's spokesman, said Russia informed the WHO as procedures require and accused the media of spreading false information.
short: The World Health Organization says it cannot fully assess the risk from the suspected plague death of a 28-year-old technician at an anti-plague laboratory in Siberia. Russia says she died of pneumonia of unknown cause.
